Far West Contractors is a commercial construction company and general contractor headquartered in Placentia, California Founded in 2009, the company specializes in SCIF(Sensitive Compartmented Information Facilities) construction projects for high-security facilities, as well as tenant improvements in the aerospace and defense industry. Their well-known project partners and clients include Boeing, Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL), and Northrop Grumman

Adams Warehouse & Delivery, Inc. — a family-owned freight and logistics company operating 11 warehouse facilities in the Houston metro area since 1976.

The dataset includes complete server backup mirrors from multiple drives (D:, E:, Data, Network Shares), capturing the company's entire digital footprint:

airq-ad.com AirQ UAE drone manufacturer founded in 2021 in Masdar City, Abu Dhabi, producing unmanned aerial systems fully in-house. It was started by Croatian entrepreneurs Dino Dedić as CEO and Igor Pongrac as CTO, who previously worked at Rimac Automobili, and has grown from 6 people to about 100 engineers. The flagship product is the Harara modular VTOL drone, carrying 6 kg of payload and flying up to 7 hours or 600 km in hybrid mode, with over 1000 test flights completed. Other products include the StingJet reusable jet target drone for air defense training and the world's first fully electric UAV launcher. The company is backed by Abu Dhabi institutions such as Tawazun Council and Masdar City Free Zone and runs real operations like medical blood sample delivery between hospitals. Its main strengths are full in-house composite production and dual defense plus commercial markets, while the main risks are its young age, ongoing aviation certification and dependence on UAE defense.

wellingtoncollege.ac.th Wellington College Bangkok is a British international school for ages 2 to 18, opened in 2018 as part of Wellington College UK, with around 1100 students on a 28 acre campus in eastern Bangkok. The curriculum runs from the English National Curriculum to IGCSE and A Levels, with the first graduating class in 2026. Fees range from about 639000 baht per year in pre nursery up to 1283500 baht in Year 12, plus a 225000 baht registration fee and a 175000 baht refundable deposit. Results are elite level with 80 percent A star or A at IGCSE and every graduate of 2026 admitted to their first choice university including Stanford, Yale and Imperial College. Admissions are selective with CAT4 testing and interviews, and strong English is required from Year 10. The school is famous for its Olympic pool, FIFA standard pitch, 600 seat theatre, wellbeing curriculum and scholarships in music, swimming, golf and academics.

giodentalspa.com Gio Dental & Med Spa  private dental and aesthetic clinic founded around 2006 in Ciudad Juárez, Mexico, targeting patients from the US border region of El Paso and Las Cruces. The practice has about 6 employees and estimated annual revenue of roughly 430000 dollars, making it a small self-owned business with no external funding. Its business model is built on cross-border dental tourism, accepting American HMO and PPO insurance and transporting patients from El Paso directly to the clinic. Core services are dental implants, orthodontics, endodontics, veneers and oral surgery, plus a med spa division with botox, fillers and physiotherapy. The clinical founder and director is Dr. Mauro D. Álvarez, an implantology specialist, working with a team of about five additional dentists. The company is positioned on price: complex dental procedures cost a fraction of US rates while offering full-service treatment and aftercare for American patients.

firstdentalhealth.com First Dental Health, Inc. dental consulting company founded in 1995 and based in Sacramento, California. It is led by Chairman and CEO Michael Zhang together with founder Dr. Rick Kershner, a periodontist who previously worked with Western Dental, Coast Dental and Pacific Dental Services. The company transforms existing dental practices of 40 to 250 chairs through leadership development, culture building and operational excellence, typically raising performance by 40 to 80 percent within 2 to 4 years. Its flagship case is Sacramento Dentistry Group, which grew from around 330000 dollars monthly revenue in 2014 to roughly 640000 dollars by 2023. It also runs a DSO consolidation model that merges 6 to 10 practices under one brand with owners keeping equity and a 3 to 7 year exit path. The team has built 14 companies that made the Inc. 5000 list, positioning it as a small but high-impact operator in US dental business consulting.

Data-Core Systems is an IT consulting and technology services company incorporated in 1988. It helps organizations with digital transformation, SAP implementation, AI and machine learning, data analytics, cloud migration, application development, publishing, and business process solutions. It serves industries including healthcare, manufacturing, government, finance, retail, and energy.

martinllp.net Martin LLP Martin LLP is a boutique business law firm founded in 1996, with offices in Stamford and New York. It focuses on middle-market companies, private equity sponsors, lenders, and business owners. Core practices: M&A and private equity, banking and finance, commercial litigation, and commercial real estate. The firm positions itself as partner-led, with small teams and senior lawyers doing hands-on work on deals from a few million to several hundred million dollars. Its people come from large national firms like Skadden, Latham & Watkins, Mayer Brown, and Schulte Roth. It publishes actively on M&A topics, notably representation and warranty insurance (RWI). It is recognized in regional rankings such as Best Law Firms 2026 for Corporate Law in Stamford.

map.ch MAP SA Swiss communications agency in Cossonay, Vaud (UID CHE-106.859.955), operating since 1968 as a business; the current legal entity was registered in 1981. It's a ~13-person full-service shop covering brand strategy, SEO/SEA, social media, and event management. Leadership: Sébastien Graap (took over 2003) and Caroline Müller (partner since 2008). Only revenue figure ever made public is ~CHF 2M for 2010; no current financials are disclosed anywhere. Core clients are French-speaking Swiss SMEs and public bodies — CarPostal, Transports publics de la région lausannoise, La Source, Yverdon Énergies, Changins. A separate training arm, map.academy, publishes rates (CHF 800–3,900 packages, CHF 1,200/day, CHF 890/month coaching); agency project work is quote-only. Portfolio runs ~30 cases with claimed results (e.g. 7% energy savings, 1,200+ event visitors)

suhaiseguranca.com.br Suhai Segurança Pessoal Brazilian personal security company founded in 1992 — one of the older, established firms in its niche. Core business: bodyguard/executive protection, family and residential security, security drivers, and corporate guarding, delivered nationwide. Teams are described as vetted, licensed professionals backed by 24/7 monitoring and in-house tactical training. The firm claims ISO 9001 and Great Place to Work certification, but doesn't publish certificates — claims are self-reported. No revenue, pricing, or verified headcount is public; everything is custom-quoted per job. Critically: since Brazil's 2024 law, security work is only legal if the firm holds a current federal police permit for that specific service and state — confirm yours before hiring. Also beware the unrelated "Suhai" auto insurer sharing the name — most complaints you'll find online are about insurance, not this company.

sbiav.com SBI Audiovisuel is a Quebec AV company founded in 1991 (HQ in Saint-Bruno-de-Montarville, ~11 staff), doing corporate event production — sound, lighting, video, webcasting — plus its signature niche: live streaming of surgical operations for medical training. It deploys its own CASTER mobile system and claims exclusive North American rights to France's Medinbox tech, which is used at hospitals like Mount Sinai NY; note SBI is an integrator, not the tech's manufacturer. Public activity runs from 2018 through 2026 (US tours, medical congresses, hiring), with no lawsuits or scam signs found. Revenue is not disclosed — third-party estimates vary ($1–5M range), all unverified. Weak spots: no independent client reviews, no published certificates, and the site blurs its own brand with Medinbox's. For Quebec/Canada corporate events or live-surgery broadcasts it's a credible pick; for critical projects, verify team size, redundancy plans, and patient-data handling in writing.

saga-u.ac.jp Saga University is a national Japanese university in Saga Prefecture, Kyushu — founded in 1949 (roots back to 1875), merged with Saga Medical School in 2003, operating as a national university corporation since 2004. Scale: ~6,600 students, ~3,300 staff, 6 faculties (including medicine with a ~600-bed hospital) across Honjo, Nabeshima, and Arita campuses. Annual revenue ¥44B ($300M), ~57% of it generated by the university hospital; state capital ¥47.3B, with a +¥1.6B surplus in FY2024. Signature strength: the Institute of Ocean Energy (IOES) — a world leader in OTEC (ocean thermal energy), pursuing the world's first 1-MW commercial plant ~2026-27 with Mitsui O.S.K. Lines. Rector since Oct 2025: Koichi Node (cardiologist); 2026 launches include Japan's first national-university cosmetic science program (30 students, 7x oversubscribed) and a joint teacher-training degree with Kumamoto University. Weak points: rankings have slid for a decade (QS Asia 801-850, THE 1501+)

netcoreunbxd.com Netcore Unbxd AI product-discovery platform for enterprise e-commerce: smart site search, 1:1 personalization, recommendations, visual intelligence ("Complete the Look"), catalog enrichment, and — its 2026 bet — a Shopping Agent (agentic commerce). Owned by India's Netcore Cloud since March 2022 (~$100M deal, 90%), run by founders Pavan Sondur and Prashant Kumar; SaaS sits on composable, API-first infra (Cloudflare, Kubernetes, multi-region), with <10ms response on 95% of queries and 35M documents processed monthly. Recognition: Gartner Magic Quadrant Leader 3 years running, highest "Current Offering" score in Forrester Wave Q3 2025, 7 G2 badges Summer 2025. Claimed customer results (self-reported): +38% AOV, +28% conversion, −60% null searches, −53% bounce. Positioning is sharply anti-native-search and anti-generic-AI, aimed at retail merchandisers with no-code workbenches and full override control. Site's main CTA is a free "personalized site experience audit."

regio-nord.com REGiO-Nord mbH (HRB 1203, Amtsgericht Neuruppin) is a municipal regional-development company in Gransee, Brandenburg, founded 2008–2009 to run the shared "Mittelzentrum" of Gransee–Zehdenick–Fürstenberg/Havel. It is 100% publicly owned (Zehdenick 1/3, Fürstenberg 1/3, Gransee 1/6, Amt Gransee 1/6), led by sole managing director Olaf Bechert with a staff of ~5 plus two tourist info offices. Its real money flows through the Kooperationsfonds — ~€8.9M in projects since 2008, with €538K spent in 2025 and €563K budgeted for 2026, of which €312K funds the company's own coordination work. Four workstreams: education (teacher recruitment, apprenticeship exchange), economy (business services, doctor recruitment, arztidylle.de), tourism (two info stations, region portals, RegioApp), and regional marketing (REGiO-Card, library network). Finances are project-transparent (open budget reports) but the GmbH's own annual accounts are only public through 2022 — request 2023–2025.

museumsiam.org Museum Siam museum in Bangkok run by NDMI under the public organization OKMD — the .org domain is real, but it's a government institute, not a private company. It occupies the former Ministry of Commerce building (1921–1922) and opened as a museum on 2 April 2008. The core exhibit Decoding Thainess (14 rooms on how Thai identity was formed) has run since 2017; there's also a free Underground Museum at MRT Sanam Chai (2020). Attendance is ~250–343K per year (different counting methods), 3.8M over 17 years; museum-level revenue isn't disclosed — finances publish only at OKMD level. Tickets: 100 THB adult, 50 students, free for kids under 15, 60+, monks, disabled visitors; open Tue–Sun 10:00–18:00. Beyond exhibits: a 4,000+ resource library, digital archives, venue rental (5–80K THB), and a nationwide museum-network support program.

skincenter.com Skin Center dermatology clinic in Fort Lauderdale, FL (6550 N Federal Hwy, Suite 320) with 40+ years of practice roots (formerly Dr. Roger Stewart's clinic, led by Dr. Barry Galitzer since the 2010s). Full spectrum: medical dermatology, Mohs surgery for skin cancer, cosmetic injectables/lasers (Botox, CoolSculpting, Ultherapy, Fraxel), an Acne Center, aesthetics, and massage. The hidden headline: since 2021 it's owned by Forefront Dermatology (125+ clinics, backed by Canadian pension fund OMERS Private Equity) — billing, records, and HR run through the network, not the local brand. Doctors rate excellent (Galitzer 4.7/5 on Healthgrades; Castle Connolly Top Doctor), but admin/office process is the weak spot — complaints cite long waits, forgotten patients, and a brusque bedside manner. Team: ~10 providers (Galitzer, Fien, Perrotto, Soro, White, Brown + PAs), plus a second office in Pompano Beach; 200+ patients/day, 10,000 sq ft.

kasetbrand.co.th Thai Ha PCL (SET: KASET) is a Thai public company founded 1993, listed since 2005, exporting jasmine rice, mung bean noodles, and snacks (brands KASET, SMART CHEF, IMPERIAL TASTE) to 80+ countries — the US is its largest market (902+ shipments, active as of Oct 2026). Core assets: a rice mill in Nakhon Pathom (100K tons/yr capacity) and a noodle factory in Nakhon Sawan; certified BRC Grade A+, US FDA, Halal, KOSHER, SMETA. The family Tangpiroonthum controls ~42% via Cheer Group Holdings, CEO Somroek Tangpiroonthum in place since 2004. But financially it's been bleeding: revenue fell from ฿611M (2020) to ฿302M (2025), six consecutive years of losses totaling ~฿330M, negative operating cash flow, debt/equity ~143%. A turnaround plan launched in 2024 — including halving par value (฿1.00→฿0.50) to wipe ~฿139M accumulated deficit — is narrowing losses (Q2 2026 −66% YoY) but the company is still unprofitable.

inovarpackaging.com Inovar Packaging Group (Irving, TX) is a PE-backed buy-and-build platform producing pressure-sensitive labels, shrink sleeves, flexible packaging, and RFID — 14 US plants, 12+ acquisitions since 2016 (latest: Kiliper Corp, Feb 2026). Owned by Kelso & Company since May 2022 (previously AEA Investors); CEO/Chairman Jeff Brezek leads, with deal advisors Milbank and Mesirow confirming real M&A scale. Revenue is private and undisclosed — realistic estimates put it at $100–250M, with ~500–750 employees (Form 5500 filings show plan participants growing 121→743 in 2020–2024). Certifications are strong: ISO 9001/14001, first US printer with GMI Platinum (both digital + flexo; serves CVS, Target, Walgreens, Home Depot), FDA 21 CFR 11 / EU Annex 11, EcoVadis Gold; won the 2024 TLMI Eugene Singer Award. Clients: food & beverage, healthcare, ag-chem, supplements, personal care — with built-in redundancy across plants for continuity.

engineersireland.ie Engineers Ireland Ireland's national professional body for engineers, founded 1835 with a Royal Charter (1877) and statutory authority under a 1969 Act to award the "Chartered Engineer" (CEng) title. HQ at 22 Clyde Road, Ballsbridge, Dublin 4; ~30,000 members (21,052 paying) across 35 regional/divisional sectors. Revenue ~€7.6M (2024) with ~€0.7M surplus and a ~€5M investment portfolio; ~49 staff, over 500 volunteers. Core functions: CEng accreditation, education program recognition (194 accredited university programs, Washington Accord member), mandatory CPD (35 hrs/yr), annual Salary Survey, and policy advocacy. President 2025–26 is John Jordan; new Director General Áine Myler started August 2026 (previously led Society of Chartered Surveyors Ireland). Membership fees run €80–€495/year by grade; the profession it represents is ~98,000 engineers contributing €12.65B to the economy, but the country faces a shortfall of ~6,000 engineers/year through 2030.

northbridge.com North Bridge Venture Partners one of Boston's most storied venture capital firms, founded in 1994 by Bill Geary, Doug Kingsley, Ed Anderson, Mike Pehl, and Richard D'Amore — ~$3.5B under management across 8 funds, ~200+ investments, 100+ exits, and 14 unicorns. Legendary portfolio: Demandware (sold to Salesforce for $2.8B), Starent Networks ($2.9B to Cisco), Proto Labs (IPO), Couchbase ($1.5B to Haveli, 2025), Quora, Salsify, Acquia ($1B to Vista), Actifio (to Google), Paydiant (to PayPal). Its growth-equity arm split off in 2018 as Guidepost Growth Equity ($1.1B+ AUM). Today the fund is in harvest mode — no new deals since 2021–2022, small remaining team, minimal website. May 2026: ransomware group DragonForce claimed to have stolen 22.9GB of internal files (unconfirmed by the firm). For startups seeking capital it's not an active option; for portfolio/LP diligence or the breach, it remains relevant.

songwooi.co.kr SONGWOOI (Song Woo Industrial Co., Ltd.,) South Korean manufacturer of automotive and industrial rubber hoses — intercooler/TCI, heater, fuel, CPF/DPF, and power steering lines — founded 1998 in Busan, HQ and plant in Yangsan since 2002. Founder-Chairman Park Su-kon localizated TCI hoses that were 100% imported from Japan, claiming 90% Korean market share; customers include Hyundai, Kia, Renault Samsung, Hyundai Heavy Industries, and Volvo CE. Certifications: IATF 16949, ISO 14001, ISO 9001; Plus Inno-Biz/Main-Biz status and national awards (Bronze Tower Medal 2015 to Park). Revenue ₩69.9B ($50M) in 2025, down from ₩104.8B peak (2013) — declining four years straight as the industry shifts to EVs — but profitability improved (5.2% operating margin, ROE 23%). Financials are unusually strong: zero debt, 80% equity ratio, ₩52.9B total assets; ~163–197 employees. Watch-outs: some databases list a different CEO (Park Eun-chul)

ptelcom.com Petroleum Telcom, Inc. (dba Telcom, Inc. / Telcom Communications) Southern California communications integrator founded in 1978 in Oxnard, CA — specializing in two-way radio for police/fire, microwave links, fiber optics, cell towers, and FCC licensing. Owned and led by Frank R. Hines (president since 1986), now a lean ~6-person shop (peak 35 in 1999), dealer for Motorola, Kenwood, and Bendix-King, with ~200 owned repeaters across CA/NV/AZ/UT. CA contractor license #620689 (B + C7) active since 1991, zero complaints, bonded and insured. Government track record is real and documented: Ventura County since 1982, Stanislaus County $1.2M, Port of LA police radio system $1.19M (2017–19), City of Oxnard up to $900K (2023–27), USGS, and 5 DoD contracts. Revenue not disclosed (est. $1–5M).

axlelogistics.com Axle Logistics non-asset freight brokerage founded in 2012 in Knoxville, Tennessee, by Drew Johnson and Jon Clay — two University of Tennessee grads who started with two people and one trucking software license. It organizes truckload, LTL, intermodal, and port drayage shipments across the US, Canada, and Mexico by matching loads with third-party carriers, focusing on Fortune 500 shippers and mid-market brands. Revenue exploded from $80M (2018) to over $1.2B gross / $159M net (2025), and headcount grew from 2 to roughly 700 — making it one of the fastest-scaling brokers in the country. It's landed on the Inc. 5000 list over a decade straight, ranked #52 among Transport Topics' top 50 logistics companies, and won Knoxville Top Workplaces seven years running. The company invested $38M in a gleaming new 84,000 sq ft HQ with state support and pays employees an average of ~$117K/year. It's a brokerage, not a carrier — so shipment quality depends on the carriers.

caspapermill.com C.A.S. Paper Mill Co., Ltd. is a Thai paper manufacturer in Singburi (est. 1990, operating since 1994), part of the Charoen Aksorn Group — Thailand's largest paper distributor, backed by Bangkok Bank and Vacharaphol. It produces 130,000 MT/yr of newsprint, printing and kraft paper plus 30,000 MT/yr of tissue (Toscotec line, 2022), from 100% recycled US/Canadian waste paper. Zero-liquid-discharge since 1994, 10 MWp floating solar; ISO 9001/14001/45001, TIS 758, FSC C125297. Exports: Vietnam, Philippines, Pakistan. Revenue est. $80–150M (~300 staff), but fell ~10% in 2025 as newsprint demand declines. Main red flag: 2018 villagers' protest over alleged coal pollution affecting 10,000+ residents, and denial of a license for the coal expansion.

stpeters.sa.edu.au St Peter's Anglican Grammar independent Anglican co-ed school in Campbelltown, NSW (est. 1983, revived parish school), teaching Pre-K to Year 6 (~428 students, ICSEA 1118 — 89th percentile nationally). It's part of the Campbelltown Anglican Schools Council (CASC) alongside Broughton Anglican College (P–12) and St Peter's Heart (special needs). Academics are solid: NAPLAN scores run ~33 points above the national average, SchoolRank rates it 69.3/100 ("Good", 129th in NSW), and it's one of only two IB PYP World Schools in the Macarthur region. Fees are modest — $9,400/yr (K–2) and $9,920/yr (Y3–6) — with generous sibling discounts up to 100%. Led by Principal Michelle McDonnell (2023–) under CEO Andrew Middleton; 39 teachers, 14.9:1 ratio, strong specialist programs (German, French, STEAM from K). The one major controversy: in July 2022 the council abruptly closed a just-launched high school (Years 7–12)

pantanalagricola.com.br Pantanal Agrícola S.A. is a Brazilian agri-input distributor (crop protection, fertilizers, seeds) founded in 2001 in São Gabriel do Oeste, Mato Grosso do Sul — 19 legal units, 15-16 stores across MS/MT/GO, ~300 employees, serving 64+ municipalities and 5 million hectares of farmland. Partners include BASF, Corteva, FMC, Sumitomo, ICL, and Brevant; the business model centers on barter (inputs repaid with grain) plus agronomic advisory. The headline event: Bunge signed an MOU in Nov 2021 to acquire a minority stake, adding grain-storage and trading muscle. It finances heavily through agri-receivables certificates (8 CRA/CDCA deals since 2019, ~R$217M+, incl. R$145M in 2025 via Ecoagro and a tokenized CDCA with Banco BV). Corporate governance is professionalizing — SA fechada since 2019, board expanded with independents in 2025-26, new CFO Flávio Sales (2025); founder-CEO Jonis Assmann still leads, with second generation (Bruno Franciosi) in management.

ak-sladek_cz Sladek & Partners Prague law firm operating as Mgr. Ivana Sládková, advokát (IČO 66252946), with 24 years of practice since 2002 — specializing in real estate transactions, divorce/family law, and attorney escrow (advokátní úschova). The firm's flagship claim: 500M CZK ($23M) held in escrow annually across 100+ segregated accounts, backed by 500M CZK insurance and 2–5 day payout guarantees. Led by Ivana Sládková (ČAK ev. č. 09496, Charles University, licensed for escrow since 2002, speaks English/German/Russian), with a tiny 3–5 person team (accountant + secretary). Listed in EPRAVO.CZ's notable law firm yearbooks (2013, 2016); pricing is quote-only (hourly/fixed/contingency), no published rates.

jjsjustice.com JJS Justice (Janet, Janet & Suggs, LLC) is a national plaintiff-side firm based in Baltimore/Pikesville, MD, founded 1996 (practice since 1978) — specializing in birth injuries/CP, medical malpractice, sexual abuse (clergy, USC/Johns Hopkins), mass torts, and whistleblower cases. Record: $3B+ in verdicts and settlements over 40 years, including the largest US sexual-abuse settlement ($852M vs. USC/Dr. Tyndall, 2021), $190M vs. Johns Hopkins, $225M NJ v. ExxonMobil, and multiple record birth-injury verdicts. Led since Sept 2025 by Andrew S. Janet after founder Howard A. Janet died at 70; core team includes Kenneth M. Suggs (ex-ATLA president) and Dr. Giles Manley (OBGYN turned lawyer). Chambers USA Band 2 (MD plaintiffs), Best Lawyers "Lawyer of the Year" 2025, Super Lawyers, Lawdragon 500, AV Preeminent, ABOTA. Contingency model (no fee unless they win), 10+ states + DC, ~17 lawyers, ~60 staff.

svmottawa.ca  ServiceMaster of Ottawa Canadian property restoration and commercial cleaning company (legal entity 1351120 Ontario Inc.), a ServiceMaster franchise since 1969 — owned since 2006 by John Cooke. HQ at 180 Wescar Lane, Ottawa (Carp/Richmond), ~140 staff, 24/7/365 emergency service across the National Capital Region. Core: water/fire/mold remediation, asbestos removal, reconstruction, odor control, janitorial — backed by IICRC techs, HCRA license B62544, Tarion, WSIB+liability, Restore 365/Xactimate. Record: 40,000+ customers served; Cooke won ServiceMaster's "Brand Ambassador of the Year" 2026, "Mid-Market Business of the Year" (Ottawa Chamber, 2008). Reputation mixed (3.8–4.3/5, 313+ reviews) — excellent on small jobs and named techs (Ryan Potestio, Jeff Jerome)

entrysystems.com Entry Systems Garage Doors & Gates 3rd-generation family business in Laguna Hills, CA (with a second design center in Tustin, opened 2024) — servicing garage doors and automated gates across South Orange County since 1972. Legal entity: Laguna Niguel Garage Door Service, Inc.; CA contractor license #916334 (class D28, active through 2028, clear record), bonded and insured. Services: garage door repair/installation (CHI, Amarr, Clopay), openers (Genie, Liftmaster, smart home), swing/slide gates (DoorKing, Elite, Eagle, solar), telephone entry systems, welding, and maintenance — same-day emergency service typical.

europassistance.co.za Europ Assistance South Africa South African emergency-assistance and insurance-administration company founded 1984 in Roodepoort, Gauteng — ~500 staff, FSCA licensed (FSP 5001), Level 1 B-BBEE, handling 1.3M calls/yr through 8,000+ providers. Key structural change: it completed a management buyout from French parent Europ Assistance (Generali Group) in late 2023 and rebranded to AZOZA in Oct 2025 — no longer part of the global Europ Assistance network (which itself merged into Generali's Redion platform in 2026). Services: roadside assistance, home emergency callouts, travel/motor claims administration, funeral cover, and white-label BPO for underwriters (Regent, Old Mutual, ABSA, Santam, Profmed, BMW, Eqstra). Led by CEO Lynette Mutsekwa (since 2023), CCO Nelson Soares. Reputation is split: B2B clients and 8,000 supplier-partners rate them well (12–20-year relationships)

otsuka.com.tw Revenue $278.3 Million Otsuka Pharmaceutical (Taiwan) Co., Ltd. Taiwanese arm of Japan's Otsuka Holdings (TSE: 4578), operating since 1974 — first as a JV, wholly owned since 1995. HQ in Taipei's Daan District with plants in Guandu and Kaohsiung, ~500–1,000 staff, capital NT$531M, president Ryoichi Fukumoto. Core business: prescription drugs (Abilify, Mucosta, nephrology/oncology lines), consumer brands (Pocari Sweat, Nature Made, CalorieMate, SOYJOY), medical devices, and a new insurance services arm. The group posted record 2025 pharma results (+22% revenue, +43% operating profit) across 84+ countries. Taiwan-specific financials aren't published (subsidiary of a listed parent), but the entity has 52 years on the market, TFDA-registered products, and a solid employer brand with active hiring since 2024.

climedi.com.br CLIMEDI  private multidisciplinary medical clinic and diagnostic center in Aracaju, Sergipe, Brazil — founded 5 Oct 1977 by Dr. João Antônio Macedo Santana (endocrinologist & nuclear medicine physician, UFS professor, SUNY Upstate NY–trained). Family-run (Santana-Macedo dynasty: João, son Gustavo, daughter Sara), with 76–121 staff, 50+ physicians across 3 units. Its unique regional edge: full nuclear medicine — PET-CT, scintigraphy, and I-131 thyroid cancer therapy with 5 CNEN-compliant isolation suites — plus 20+ specialties (endocrinology, cardiology, gastro, mastology, orthopedics, ENT, neuro) and complete diagnostics (MRI, CT, mammography, endoscopy, bone densitometry, 54+ tests). Quality credentials: PNCQ "Excelente" (highest tier), SBAC, DICQ; registered in CNES, works with SUS, private insurers, and union health plans (APCEF+). Government payments total R$ 11M+ (Portal da Transparência); private revenue undisclosed (est. R$ 20–50M/yr).

upf.br Universidade de Passo Fundo private community philanthropic university in Passo Fundo, Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil — founded 1968 (Decree 62.835), run by the FUPF foundation, with 7 campuses, ~10,000 students, 486 professors (48% PhD), and 100,000+ alumni. It holds the maximum MEC institutional rating (5), ranks 6th among Brazil's best private universities and 5th in research nationally (RUF 2025), and is in the THE World 2026 ranking and top-300 globally for sustainability (GreenMetric). Flagships: Medicine (MEC concept 5, expanding from 750 to 2,000 students with R$ 60M invested), Pharmacy (MEC 5), Veterinary (Hospital Veterinário + 170-ha Cepagro), Engineering (chemical #5 nationally), and Law (70 years old). Financially healthy — R$ 60M annual surplus, independent audits published, board with civil-society oversight; ~70% of students get aid (ProUni, Bolsa Filantropia, FIES, CrediUPF). New rector for 2026–2030: Edison Alencar Casagranda (93% of votes, took office July 2026).

campbellrhea.com Campbell Rhea US manufacturer of laboratory and educational casework — legal entity Institutional Casework, Inc. (ICI) — with roots to 1951 in Paris, TN. The brand survived a 2005 tornado that destroyed its former parent Mohon International, was relaunched by local investors in 2006 (CEO Jim Arthurs ever since), and acquired Jamestown Metal Products (NY) plus a steel plant in Union City, TN — 650,000 sq ft of manufacturing total. Products: wood/steel/stainless lab casework, ISOLATOR fume hoods, countertops, athletic lockers (Olympian), Patriot tables — certified SEFA-8, FSC, AIA CES. Revenue $32.1M (2025) per FDMC 300, down from a $63.5M COVID-era peak (2022); ~250 employees, 35+ US dealers, projects at Penn State, UC Davis, Vanderbilt, Case Western, U of Missouri.

dentistryofnewportbeach.com Newport Beach Dentistry family dental practice in Newport Beach, CA (1401 Avocado Ave, Ste 209), founded 30+ years ago and currently run by brothers Dr. F. Frank Foroutan (USC DDS 1998) and Dr. F. Ryan Foroutan (USC DDS 1996) — a practice that changed ownership from Dr. Rasch → Kantor/Appelsies → Foroutan over the decades. Services: implants, crowns, veneers, Invisalign, root canals, periodontics, extractions, sedation, whitening, emergency care (same-day); accepts Delta Dental Premier/PPO and most major insurance, CareCredit financing; $99 new-patient special (exam + X-rays + cleaning). Team ~10 (Nancy — office manager, Monica — front desk, Erica — hygienist); languages: English, Farsi, Spanish. Related entities: Foroutan Dental Inc. (Buena Park), OC Elite Dental (Buena Park + Anaheim Hills); also connected to F. Foroutan DDS Inc. (Corona). No revenue disclosed (private practice, est. $2–5M/yr for 3 doctors in this location).

tulsat.com TULSAT leading US distributor and repair center for cable TV (CATV) equipment — headend gear, fiber nodes, amplifiers, taps, power supplies — founded 1985 by brothers David and Ken Chymiak in Broken Arrow, OK (100,000+ sq ft). From a bankruptcy buyout it became exclusive Master Distributor and authorized service center for Scientific-Atlanta (now Cisco), plus Motorola/Arris, CommScope, ATX, Quintech. It merged into public ADDvantage Technologies (NASDAQ: AEY) in 1999 (peak revenue $50.3M in 2005), then the cable segment was bought back by David Chymiak's Leveling 8 Inc. for $10.3M in 2019 — private again. Today: ~25 staff, est. ~$10M revenue; group includes NCS Industries (PA), ComTech Services (MO), Tulsat-Atlanta (GA), Nave Communications (MD), Triton Datacom (FL). Core value: largest legacy/obsolete CATV parts inventory + factory-authorized repair, a lifeline for aging networks as cord-cutting shrinks the industry.

sharedmedtech.com Shared Medical Technology, Inc. US medical equipment rental and service company founded in 2004, HQ in Schenectady, NY — 7 offices (NY, MA, VA), ~40–50 staff, no external funding raised. Core business: urgent rental of patient monitors, ventilators, CPAP, ultrasound, portable X-ray, infusion pumps, and bariatric/XL beds and chairs — plus a niche no competitor claims to cover: State Regulatory Compliance certification for transporting XL/bariatric patients across 10+ states (vehicle inspections, certified safe transport). Real clients include Albany Medical Center, OrthoNY, Saratoga Surgery Center, Community Care Physicians, and Brooklyn Surgery Center. Self-developed logistics platform.

sbendo.com Santa Barbara Endodontics solo specialty practice of Dr. Terrell F. Pannkuk, DDS, MScD — one of the most credentialed endodontists in the US — at 9 E Pedregosa St, Santa Barbara, CA, operating since 1987 (39 years). Pannkuk is a Diplomate of the American Board of Endodontics (since 1988), volunteer clinical professor at UCSF, peer reviewer for the Journal of Endodontics, founding president of the Schilder Institute, founder of Pure Dental Learning, and author of a chapter in Ingle's Endodontics (7th ed.) — peers call him "the endodontist's endodontist." Services: root canals, retreatment, apicoectomy, implants, CBCT 3D diagnostics (Carestream 9600), microscope-assisted microsurgery, same-day emergency care. Team of 5 staff.

policia.gob.ec Ecuador's National Police country's main law enforcement agency — 180 years old (institutionalized 1846, professionalized 1938), under the Ministry of Interior, commanded by GraS. Pablo Vinicio Dávila Maldonado (since July 2025). Scale: 58,000+ officers, 14 police schools, 317 per 100K population. 2025 was its most active year ever: 712,642 operations, 71,399 arrests, 227 tons of drugs seized, $9.6B in damage to criminal organizations, 21 high-value targets neutralized — but also Ecuador's deadliest year (8,847 homicides). 2026 shows improvement: −27.7% homicides, −43–56% robberies; new Dinae anti-kidnapping unit achieves 90%+ effectiveness. Budget: ~$1–1.2B/yr from state funds.
